draft.title: Chord properties
card: A chord is a straight line joining two points on a circle. A line from the centre that is perpendicular to a chord cuts the chord into two equal parts.
Example: a circle has radius 13 cm. A chord is 5 cm from the centre. Half the chord is \(\sqrt{13^{2} - 5^{2}}\), which is \(\sqrt{144} = 12\) cm, so the chord is 24 cm long.
Equal chords in a circle are the same distance from the centre. Chords that are the same distance from the centre are equal.
Two chords cross inside a circle. Each is cut into two parts. The product of the two parts of one chord equals the product of the two parts of the other: \(a \times b = c \times d\).
draft.remember: A perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord. Crossing chords: part times part is the same for both.

a.q: A line from the centre of a circle is perpendicular to a chord of length 18 cm. How long is each part of the chord?
a.why: A perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so each part is \(18 \div 2 = 9\) cm. Giving 18 cm ignores the halving, and 36 cm doubles instead of halving.
a.clue: The perpendicular from the centre cuts the chord into two equal parts.

b.q: Two chords cross inside a circle. One chord is cut into parts of 4 cm and 9 cm. The other is cut into parts of 6 cm and \(x\) cm. What is \(x\)?
b.why: The products are equal, so \(6x = 4 \times 9 = 36\), which gives \(x = 6\). Adding the parts of the first chord and subtracting 6 would give 7, and that is not how the products work.
b.clue: Set the product of one chord's parts equal to the product of the other's.

wants.brief: A circle with two chords crossing inside it. One chord is cut into parts labelled a and b, the other into parts labelled c and d, with the crossing point marked.
wants.why: It shows which parts are multiplied in the crossing chords rule.

problems.detail: Why (b) explains a wrong answer of 7 (4 + 9 − 6), but 7 cm is not among the options (6, 7.5, 2, 13). It does not explain the distractors actually shown.

A chord is called 'a straight line joining two points on a circle'. A chord is an interval (a line segment) with its endpoints on the circle. A full straight line through two points of a circle is a secant, which point 5 of this chapter covers, so the wording could blur the two terms.

b.q: Two chords cross inside a circle. One chord is cut into parts of 4 cm and 9 cm. The other is cut into parts of 6 cm and \(x\) cm. What is \(x\)?
b.why: The parts of each chord are multiplied, so \(6x = 4 \times 9 = 36\), which gives \(x = 6\). Adding the parts instead, \(4 + 9 = 6 + x\), gives 7 cm. Multiplying parts from different chords, such as \(4x = 9 \times 6\), gives 13.5 cm.
b.clue: Multiply the two parts of the same chord, then set the products equal.
